data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root 'Baydah' which means 'bright' or 'radiant'. historical_references.reference: Ibn Battuta describes a city named Bayda in his travelogue Rihla. The city was the capital of the Rasulid Dynasty in Yemen from the 13th to 15th centuries.
Al-Idrisi mentions a place called Bayda, which was an important agricultural region in the Maghreb during the 12th century. It was ruled by the Almohad Caliphate.
